title: Finite scalar restriction preserves constructible complexes and bounds
statement: Let $X$ be a Noetherian scheme, $a:A\to A'$ a homomorphism of finite commutative rings, and $a_X:A_X\to A'_X$ the induced morphism of constant ring sheaves [def-weil-pbc-constant-sheaf] on its small pro-étale site [def-weil-pbc-proetale-site]. Restriction of scalars [def-pc-sheaf-restrict-scalars] is exact on module sheaves [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category] and thus induces a termwise functor $D(a_X):D(A'_X)\to D(A_X)$ on unbounded derived categories [def-weil-abstract-derived-category]. It sends each constructible sheaf of $A'_X$-modules to a constructible sheaf of $A_X$-modules [def-weil-proetale-constructible-sheaf], using the same stratification and trivializing covers. For every $L\in D(A'_X)$ and $q\in\mathbf Z$, $H^q(D(a_X)L)\cong\operatorname{Res}_{a_X}H^q(L)$. In particular it preserves bounded constructibility and preserves and reflects vanishing of cohomology in each degree. Surjectivity of $a$ is not assumed.

proof.text: Use the existing additive restriction functor and its named finite-limit and finite-colimit preservation theorems from [def-pe-proetale-ring-restrict-scalars]. Its composite with the faithful underlying abelian-sheaf functor is definitionally the original underlying abelian-sheaf functor, so restriction is faithful. Thus it preserves and reflects zero objects, by the identity-equals-zero criterion.

source.place: Tag 03DA, lemma-abelian; kernel and cokernel constructions immediately preceding it.

proof.text: Prove naturality of the canonical constant-ring direct-image map by the sheafification universal property: both composites agree after the constant-presheaf unit. Counit naturality then gives naturality of the coefficient inverse-image map. For a stratum immersion, use [lem-pur-proetale-constant-coefficient-comparison] for both rings. The resulting coefficient square satisfies the hypotheses of the ordinary invertible restriction/pullback comparison in [lem-weil-pbc-ring-sheaf-change-adjunction]. Its component identifies pullback of scalar restriction with scalar restriction of pullback. Localization over any covering object commutes with restriction definitionally.

source.place: Tag 03D2, lemma-pullback-module (apply inverse image to the action); Tag 03D3, lemma-adjoint-push-pull-modules; constant sheaves in Tag 093I, section-constant.

proof.text: Prove compatibility of simultaneous ring/module sheafification with any commuting coefficient square. Map the scalar-restricted presheaf to the restricted sheafification using the original module unit; linearity is exactly the coefficient square. Lift by [lem-cbc-sieve-module-sheafification]. Under the faithful underlying abelian-sheaf functor this lift is the identity, by the abelian sheafification adjunction, and hence it is invertible. Apply this to the localized constant-ring units, whose square is naturality of the constant-presheaf sheafification unit. Combine the result, the pullback comparison, and restriction of each original trivialization to prove proEtaleFiniteScalarRestriction_sameTrivializations, with precisely the original covers and scalar-restricted models.

source.place: Tag 093I, section-constant, and Tag 093Q, definition-locally-constant; the constant model with its induced scalar action.

proof.text: Apply the unchanged-trivializations theorem to the local-constancy witnesses on each original stratum. The underlying additive neighbourhood diagrams of a module sheaf and its scalar restriction are definitionally equal. Their module stalk constructions therefore have the same underlying colimit carrier. Transport finiteness through the stalk of the pullback-comparison isomorphism. This proves proEtaleFiniteScalarRestriction_sameStratification. The intrinsic constructibility definition already assumes finite underlying stalk sets, so no separate finite-generation theorem is needed. Retain the original stratification and its positive number of strata to obtain preservation of constructibility.

source.place: Tag 09AJ, definition-constructible; apply its locally constant finite-type condition using the unchanged finite stalks.

proof.text: Apply the existing exact-functor construction [lem-weil-pbc-exact-functor-derived-factorization]. The library theorem Functor.mapDerivedCategoryHomologyFunctorIso is the descended exact-complex homology comparison [lem-weil-pbc-exact-functor-complex-cohomology]. Its inverse has exactly the direction of the stated natural isomorphism. Pin the module-category and localization universes to the universes already fixed by the statement; this introduces no bound on complexes.

source.place: Tag 015F, lemma-right-derived-exact-functor, especially (3)-(4); cohomology comparison from homology.tex Tag 010N, lemma-exact-functor.

proof.text: For each degree, transport zero through the homology comparison. Restriction preserves zero because it is additive, and reflects zero by faithfulness and the identity-equals-zero criterion. Extract the original lower and upper t-structure bounds and apply this degreewise equivalence with DerivedCategory.isGE_iff and isLE_iff, keeping the same bounds. Transport constructibility through the homology comparison: pullback, localization, and the geometric module stalk are functorial, so isomorphisms transport both local trivializations and finite stalks without changing a chosen stratification. This completes proEtaleFiniteScalarRestriction_constructible.

The statement is unchanged; the added stmt_dep def-weil-pbc-bounded-derived-subcategories is needed for 'bounded constructibility'. The statement is a true generalization of the source sentence in main-20261015 sk-prop-integral-criterion-reductions.proof.md, second paragraph, last sentence ('restriction of scalars, which preserves constructibility'): it allows any homomorphism of finite commutative rings, and the parent det-prop-integral-criterion-reductions step 4 uses it for the quotients Λ_n→Λ_{n-1} and Λ_n→Λ_1. Both coefficient rings are constant ring sheaves on the same small pro-étale site; no completed coefficients are mixed in. Steps: (1) exactness and zero reflection follow from def-pc-sheaf-restrict-scalars (same underlying abelian sheaf) and lem-weil-pbc-module-sheaves-colimits-forgetful(1). (2) I checked the square c_{A'}∘i^{-1}a_X = a_Z∘c_A on constant sections, using prop-weil-pbc-proetale-constant-ring-map, which allows any morphism and the empty scheme; the two A_Z-actions on i^{-1}M agree because of this square. (3) For the constant models, lem-cbc-sieve-module-sheafification shows the underlying abelian sheafification does not depend on the ring, so Res of the constant sheaf of P is the constant sheaf of Res_a P. On the localized site the definition uses the restricted ring sheaf; this is harmless because the action is fixed by the local formula. (4) Res leaves the stalk sets unchanged; a finitely generated module over finite A' is finite, hence finitely generated over A, and the step does not assume A'-generators stay A-generators. (5) The Mathlib leaves mapDerivedCategoryFactors and homologyFunctorIso give the unbounded derived functor and the natural comparison H^q(Res L) ≅ Res H^q(L), with no resolution needed. (6) Vanishing is preserved and reflected, so bounded constructibility holds with the same interval [r,s]. Small cases checked: X empty, A'=0, the identity, Z/4→Z/2, and F_2→F_4 (non-surjective). Stacks tags checked against tags/tags: 03DA, 03D2, 03D3, 093I, 093Q, 09AJ, 015F (derived.tex:5884, unbounded clauses 3–4) and 010N. No SGA source is used.
